facts.fact: StackAdapt launched Unbiasify, a free open-source Chrome extension that removes the name and profile photo of candidates on online recruitment platforms, announced October 11, 2017.
facts.quote: continues its support for diversity in tech through the launch of “Unbiasify” an open-source project that removes the name and profile photo of candidates on online recruitment platforms.

facts.fact: Unbiasify was StackAdapt's second community-driven initiative under the #HackDiversity campaign, which was launched in June 2017.
facts.quote: Unbiasify is StackAdapt’s second community-driven initiative of #HackDiversity, a campaign launched in June 2017 raising awareness for diversity in tech.

facts.fact: An 18-minute documentary was released as part of the #HackDiversity campaign, calling for an industry effort to address bias in tech.
facts.quote: An 18 minute documentary was released calling for an industry effort to address bias in the tech industry.

facts.fact: According to StackAdapt's Director of Talent Acquisition, orchestras that introduced 'blind recruitment' in auditioning in the 1970s and 1980s increased the share of female musicians hired from 25% to 46%.
facts.quote: Orchestras introduced ‘blind recruitment’ in their auditioning process in the 1970s and 1980s and increased the number of female musicians hired from 25% to 46%.

facts.fact: Unbiasify was in full function at StackAdapt at the time of launch, and the company planned to make it available for other social media and recruitment platforms in the upcoming months.
facts.quote: Unbiasify will be made available for other social media and recruitment platforms in the upcoming months.
